video_caption: A Black woman with her hair styled in a high braided bun, wearing a white off-the-shoulder top, speaks directly to the camera with a serious yet engaging expression, occasionally making small hand gestures. She is seated in front of a white wall, with a dark wooden bookshelf filled with books on her left and a white desk with a white and gray microscope on her right. Behind her, a colorful abstract painting and a white board with diagrams are visible on the wall. Throughout the segment, several comment bubbles appear and disappear around her. From `caramel465 101` (top left): "We used baking soda and ACV to build erupting volcanoes. Can't image that would be a safe mix. Looking forward to to more videos. TFS" (meaning: "We used baking soda and apple cider vinegar to build erupting volcanoes. I can't imagine that would be a safe mix. Looking forward to more videos. Thanks for sharing."). From `ashley7` (top right): "Baking soda relaxer? I've only heard of the blue and the coconut treatment. But has no oneach in it." (meaning: "Is baking soda a hair relaxer? I've only heard of the blue and the coconut treatment. But does it have no-lye in it?"). From `nikkiaka09` (middle right): "Baking soda relaxer? Wth?" (meaning: "Baking soda as a hair relaxer? What the hell?"). From `Ore Teabe` (bottom right): "I use baking soda to exfoliate my face. Who knew people used it on HAIR? Lol" (meaning: "I use baking soda to exfoliate my face. Who knew people used it on HAIR? Laugh out loud"). From `Y.a` (bottom left): "Who ever heard of baking soda for your hair 🧐 The first word is BAKING" (meaning: "Whoever heard of baking soda for your hair? [Emoji: thinking face] The first word is BAKING"). A green "GreenBEAUTY" logo is visible in the bottom left corner of the screen.

A Black woman with her dark hair styled in a twisted high bun and wearing a white off-the-shoulder top speaks directly to the camera from 0:02 to 0:49, maintaining an informative expression and occasionally gesturing with her hands. She is positioned in a room with a dark bookshelf on her left, filled with various books and a small decorative bicycle, and a dark desk on her right, holding a silver and black microscope. On the light-colored wall behind her, two framed artworks are visible: one with a technical diagram and the other with abstract colorful shapes. At 0:17, two picture-in-picture frames appear beside her: the left frame displays a petri dish with a white foamy substance and molecular models, captioned "PRDS and CONS of using BAKING SODA on your natural hair" (Pros and Cons of using BAKING SODA on your natural hair), while the right frame shows a bowl of yellowish liquid, captioned "The Science of how APPLE CIDER VINEGAR works on natural hair." These frames disappear at 0:21 but reappear at 0:31 with new content: the left frame now shows animated hair strands in a foamy substance, captioned "PROS and CONS of use," and the right frame shows a person braiding dark natural hair, captioned "How to do a BAKING SODA relaxer (DETAILED INSTRUCTIONS)." The image in the right frame then changes to a close-up of coiled natural hair at 0:35, while the left frame shows a slightly different angle of the foamy hair animation, and both captions remain the same. The picture-in-picture frames vanish again at 0:40, and the woman continues speaking until 0:49, when the scene transitions to a white screen with a light green leaf logo forming a partial circle, beside the text "GREENBEAUTY™".

The video opens with a split screen, presenting two series of topics: "APPLE CIDER VINEGAR SERIES" on the left and "BAKING SODA SERIES" on the right. Each series features four small preview images with accompanying text. On the left, images depict a colorful dial for "The Science of how APPLE CIDER VINEGAR (ACV) REALLY works on natural hair," hands cutting apples for "How to make a better ACV RINSE from scratch," a glass jar on a scale for "How to make homemade apple cider vinegar, or an ACV RINSE," and hands stirring a pan for "Where's THE MOTHER in ACV? Is it really that important?". On the right, images show a petri dish with white substance for "PROS and CONS of using BAKING SODA on your natural hair," hands braiding hair for "How to do a BAKING SODA rinse (DETAILED INSTRUCTIONS)," and a hand spraying liquid for "BAKING SODA and ACV RINSE: Is it safe and does it work?". The scene then transitions to a dark brown background, displaying a glass bowl of amber liquid (apple cider vinegar) on the left, with the chemical formula "C₂H₄O₂ ACETIC ACID" and a 3D molecular model above it. The text "GreenBeauty" is visible on the bowl. Subsequently, the screen splits, with the apple cider vinegar on the left and a glass bowl of white powdery substance (baking soda) on the right, also accompanied by its chemical formula "NaHCO₃ SODIUM BICARBONATE" and a 3D molecular model. Text overlays on the baking soda bowl list various uses: "Polish Teeth Diaper Rash Hair Care". The left side then changes to show a clear squeeze bottle labeled "Baking Soda" and a red spray bottle labeled "ACV Rinse" under the title "Separate Method". Finally, the right side transforms to show a "Combine Method," where a hand pours amber liquid from a measuring cup into a bowl of white powder, creating a foamy, bubbling mixture labeled "Baking Soda & ACV". The video concludes with a close-up, highly magnified view of a single strand of brown hair against a white background.

The video begins with a close-up of a dark brown hair strand, appearing relatively smooth, with the "GREENBEAUTY" logo subtly displayed in the bottom left corner. Initially, the strand's surface is somewhat even, but then a microscopic view reveals its outer cuticle layers as distinct, uneven, overlapping scales that resemble shingles. These scales first appear to lift and become jagged, then smooth down, and then lift again, demonstrating their potential to change state. At the 0:14 mark, the screen splits into two, showing extreme close-ups of human fingernails. The left image displays a healthy fingernail with a smooth, well-kept cuticle, while the right image shows a dry, slightly lifted, and damaged cuticle on another nail. The hair strand, now in its smooth state, is re-introduced on the left side of the screen, alongside the healthy fingernail. The damaged fingernail then disappears, leaving the hair strand appearing smooth again. However, the hair cuticle scales quickly become extremely raised and rough, and small white, flaky particles appear to shed from its surface, symbolizing dryness and damage. Finally, a golden, oily-looking substance flows down the hair strand, causing the rough scales to smooth down and lie flat against the strand, suggesting a treatment or lubrication effect, as the "GREENBEAUTY" logo reappears.

The segment begins with a white background featuring a semi-circular pH balancing scale for hair, ranging from 0 (Acid) to 14 (Alkaline), with 7 marked as Neutral. A "safe zone" is highlighted in green and light blue, spanning pH 3 to 8. On the right, text "OPEN" appears, followed by "CLOSE." Arrows then point down from "OPEN" to "RELAX" and from "CLOSE" to "TIGHTEN," suggesting a correlation between pH levels and hair cuticle states. The image fades out. The scene then transitions to a split screen. On the left, labeled "Separate Method," a clear squeeze bottle marked "Baking Soda" and a red spray bottle labeled "ACV Rinse" are shown. On the right, labeled "Combine Method," a measuring spoon pours a yellowish liquid (presumably ACV) into a clear glass bowl containing white powder (baking soda). The mixture instantly fizzes and foams, filling the bowl, with text "Baking Soda & ACV" at the bottom right.

The video segment opens with a shot of a dark surface featuring two bottles. On the left is a clear plastic bottle with a pointed nozzle, labeled "Baking Soda." To its right is a red plastic spray bottle, labeled "ACV Rinse." Above them, the text "Separate Method" is displayed. Two rectangular insets are positioned above the bottles. The left inset initially shows a white powder with red specks in a dish, with text below reading: "PROS and CONS of using BAKING SODA on your natural hair." This inset then transitions to a word cloud, progressively revealing words like "Polish Teeth," "Hair Care," "Diaper Rash," "Relieve Skin Irritation," "DEODORANT," and "Relieve HEARTBURN." The right inset initially displays a colorful arc-shaped gauge, with text below reading: "The Science of how APPLE CIDER VINEGAR (ACV Rinse) works on natural hair." This inset then changes to an animation showing hair strands. Around the 0:10 mark, two green downward-pointing arrow icons appear below the "Baking Soda" bottle, followed by a red downward-pointing arrow icon below the "ACV Rinse" bottle. The scene then transitions to a close-up of the colorful arc-shaped gauge, which is revealed to be a "pH Balancing Scale for Hair" ranging from "Acid" (0-6) to "Neutral" (7) to "Alkaline" (8-14).

The video opens with a "pH Balancing Scale for Hair" (pH Balancing Scale for Hair) diagram, a semi-circular scale from 0 (Acid) to 14 (Alkaline) with 7 marked as Neutral and a "safe zone" highlighted in green and teal between pH 4 and 6. Baking soda is pinpointed at a pH of 9, labeled as "baking soda" and outside the safe zone, while ACV (Apple Cider Vinegar) is shown at a pH of 2, labeled "ACV" and also outside the safe zone. The narrator explains that baking soda's alkaline pH relaxes cuticles and ACV's acidic pH tightens them, suggesting a common belief in using them sequentially. The scene then transitions to a split view: on the left, a hand holds a clear plastic squeeze bottle filled with a clear liquid, labeled "Shampoo 8oz of distilled water + 1 teaspoon of baking soda pH 9," and on the right, another hand holds a red plastic spray bottle with a reddish-orange liquid, labeled "Conditioner 1oz of ACV + 7oz of distilled water pH of 3." A red triangle with the text "not in the safe zone" (not in the safe zone) points to both bottles, visually reinforcing the narrator's warning that these mixtures fall outside the hair's safe pH range and could be damaging if used regularly.

The video segment opens with a static shot featuring a clear glass bowl filled with a white powdery substance (baking soda) on the left side of the screen. The background is a dark wooden surface. On the right side, text is displayed on a dark background, titled "Baking Soda Scalp Treatment". Below the title, there is a numbered list of instructions: "1. Only once to three times a year", "2. Dilute with water", "3. Focus on your scalp, avoid hair strands", and "4. Do ACV Rinse after". A small green leaf logo is visible in the bottom left corner of the screen. At 0:16, the text on the right side is replaced by a 2x3 grid of six distinct images, while the bowl of baking soda remains on the left. These images depict various microscopic views related to hair and scalp health: the top-left image shows hair follicles being rinsed with water, creating bubbles; the top-right shows hair strands with dry, flaky material at their base; the middle-left illustrates a microscopic view of a scalp with tiny green and blue organisms; the middle-right displays a hair follicle with small, peach-colored, seed-like structures at its base; the bottom-left reveals a hair follicle with small, white, claw-like organisms (mites) attached; and the bottom-right shows another close-up of a hair follicle with similar white, elongated structures. No people are shown throughout the segment.

The video opens with a static shot of a clear glass bowl filled with a white powdery substance, possibly baking soda or a similar powder, positioned on a dark brown wooden surface. To the right of the bowl, a collage of six smaller images is displayed. These images are microscopic or highly magnified views related to hair and scalp health. The top-left image shows hair being rinsed or washed, creating a swirling effect in water. The top-right image presents a close-up of hair strands emerging from the scalp, with visible follicle structures. The middle-left image depicts a stylized microscopic view of numerous cylindrical structures, possibly hair shafts, with small green and blue spherical elements scattered among them, suggesting a treatment or interaction at a cellular level. The middle-right image offers another close-up of hair follicles, showing the hair shafts firmly rooted in the scalp. The bottom-left image shows a cluster of reddish-pink, egg-like structures nestled within a fibrous, root-like base, which could represent new hair growth or a natural ingredient. Finally, the bottom-right image displays two magnified hair follicles with their root bulbs clearly visible. In the bottom-left corner of the main frame, a green leaf logo and the text "GREENBEAUTY" are visible.

The video opens with a close-up of a clear glass bowl filled with white powder, labeled "BAKING SODA SCALP TREATMENT > SHAMPOO > ACV RINSE" at the top of the screen, against a dark wooden background. A "GreenBeauty" logo is visible in the bottom left corner. At the 0:07 mark, the screen splits into two sections: "Separate Method" on the left and "Combine Method" on the right. The left side displays a clear plastic squeeze bottle labeled "Baking Soda" (containing clear liquid) and a red plastic spray bottle labeled "ACV Rinse" (also containing clear liquid). The right side shows a glass bowl with a foamy, light yellowish liquid. The video then transitions back to a full screen view of the glass bowl containing the foamy liquid, with "Combine Method" displayed at the top and "Baking Soda & ACV" at the bottom, indicating that this is the result of mixing baking soda and apple cider vinegar.

A measuring cup pours a light brown liquid, identified by the superimposed text as apple cider vinegar, into a clear glass bowl containing a white powder, baking soda, which is denoted as NaHCO₃. Upon contact, the substances react, producing a large volume of white foam that quickly fills the bowl. As the reaction progresses, a chemical equation appears at the top right of the screen: "NaHCO₃ + C₂H₄O₂" (representing baking soda and acetic acid, respectively). This then changes to show the products: "-> NaC₂H₃O₂ + H₂CO₃" (sodium acetate and carbonic acid). Subsequently, the carbonic acid (H₂CO₃) is shown decomposing into "H₂O + CO₂" (water and carbon dioxide), with animated white gas particles visually representing the escaping carbon dioxide rising from the foam and dissipating into the air. The foam in the bowl gradually subsides as the reaction continues.

The video segment opens with a clear glass bowl containing a light brownish-yellow foamy liquid resting on a dark wooden surface. Overlaid text initially reads "NaC₂H₃O₂ + H₂O" followed by "SODIUM ACETATE", which then updates to "WATER" next to "H₂O", and finally simplifies to "SALT WATER" below the chemical formula. A hand with dark skin then dips a yellow pH test strip into the liquid. The strip, initially yellow, changes color slightly, and accompanying text at the bottom indicates "PH BETWEEN 6 AND 7". Subsequently, the strip is held against its packaging, which displays a "pH 1-14" color chart for "100 STRIPS", confirming the pH reading to be around 6 or 7. The scene transitions to an animated, semi-circular pH balancing scale for hair, ranging from 0 (Acid) to 14 (Alkaline), with 7 marked "Neutral". A green "safe zone" is indicated, and "salt water" is highlighted in light blue between pH 6 and 7. Concurrently, a list of "SALT WATER SCALP TREATMENT (BENEFITS)" appears incrementally on the right: "1. Help relieve dandruff & Seborrheic Dermatitis", "2. Detoxifying", "3. Reduces inflammation", "4. Heals wounds", and "5. Clarifies oily build-up". The "GREENBEAUTY" logo is visible in the bottom left corner throughout the segment.

The video segment features a white background displaying a colorful, arc-shaped pH balancing scale for hair, ranging from 0 (Acid) to 14 (Alkaline) with 7 marked as "Neutral." A light green-blue section on the scale, around pH 8-9, is labeled "salt water" and is within a larger "safe zone" indicated by an arc above the left side of the scale. To the right of the scale, text initially appears listing "SALT WATER SCALP TREATMENT (BENEFITS)": "1. Help relieve dandruff & Seborrheic Dermatitis", "2. Detoxifying", "3. Reduces inflammation", "4. Heals wounds", and "5. Clarifies oily build-up." Around 0:11, this list quickly morphs into a jumble of letters and then reconfigures to display "SALT WATER SCALP TREATMENT" with usage instructions: "1. Only once to four times a year", "2. Focus on your scalp, avoid hair strands", and "3. Deep condition after." The pH scale remains static throughout the segment. At the very end, "GREENBEAUTY" appears in the bottom left corner.

The video segment opens with a graphic displaying a colorful pH balancing scale for hair, ranging from 0 (Acid, red) to 14 (Alkaline, red) with 7 as neutral, highlighting a "safe zone" from pH 4-6 and "salt water" at pH 7-8. Adjacent text outlines "SALT WATER SCALP TREATMENT" instructions: "1. Only once to four times a year", "2. Focus on your scalp, avoid hair strands", and "3. Deep condition after". The scene transitions to a hand adding a white granular substance, presumably salt, from a measuring spoon into a clear glass measuring cup containing water on a dark wooden surface, then stirring it with a thin wooden stick. Next, a hand holds a pH test strip that was dipped into the salt water mixture, comparing it against a universal test paper chart, revealing the pH to be "BETWEEN 5 AND 6" (yellowish-green on the strip). A text overlay on the measuring cup then shows the recommended treatment order: "SALT WATER SCALP TREATMENT > SHAMPOO > DEEP CONDITIONER". The video then shifts to a white background, presenting three green-framed image thumbnails: the first shows a petri dish with a creamy substance and the chemical formula for baking soda, titled "PROS AND CONS of using BAKING SODA on your natural hair"; the second features a close-up of dark, braided hair, titled "How to do a BAKING SODA relaxer (DETAILED INSTRUCTIONS)"; and the third displays a white squeeze bottle and a red spray bottle, titled "BAKING SODA and ACV RINSE for rapid growth! Is it safe and does it work?". During this segment, various words related to baking soda uses, like "Polish Teeth", "Diaper Rash", and "Hair Care", briefly appear and disappear as the middle hair image changes texture. Finally, the video shows a young Black woman with her dark, curly hair styled in two space buns against a black background, looking directly at the camera with a neutral expression, with a "GREENBEAUTY" logo in the corner. The video concludes with the "GREENBEAUTY" logo on a white background, followed by social media icons and handles for Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, and Pinterest.
